reads.best: The artist and agent edit the same durable project through revision-checked routes, with undo and exports to professional editing formats.
reads.worst: The pinned distribution excludes tests, relies on private Hermes authentication imports and direct Desktop bridge access, and documents Windows-only testing.

reads.best: Creator approvals bind the reviewed tool contract, and tests cover revocation during queued dispatch, changed grants, destructive-tool rejection and separate owner/guest listeners.
reads.worst: Optional image recipes store keys outside Hermes secrets, public links default to an author-operated relay, and cloudflared is fetched from mutable releases/latest with a digest supplied by that same response.

reads.best: Charts aggregate actual rows locally, numeric remarks use computed placeholders, and proposals wait for acceptance with undo.
reads.worst: Hidden Ask sessions can use the user’s tools; avoiding writes, commands and messages is prompt advice plus approval denial, not an enforced tool allowlist.

reads.best: Very large, heavily tested codebase (about 89 test files) with a demo, screenshots and Desktop UI.
reads.worst: Huge surface (~31k lines, 18+ tools) that is hard to review and reaches many sources.

reads.best: A coherent proactive layer built on public surfaces (six tools, /ha, CLI command, system-prompt section, three hooks, cron with a no-model pulse) where money, public and irreversible cards always wait for the person.
reads.worst: The Telegram reaction handler is marked UNTESTED in the code and guesses which card a reaction answers, there is no CI, and the CLI fallback parses `hermes cron list` text with regexes.

reads.best: A genuinely new agent-native idea (the agent was in the room at 3am) with careful statistics, honest copy, screenshots and a full Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Only the statistics are tested; the per-turn injection hooks, guard and sleep-file importers are untested, it reads Hermes's private state.db schema, and plugin.yaml (0.6.0) disagrees with __version__ (0.5.1).

reads.best: It is a broad, well-documented native provider integration with schema validation, secret-store use, and extensive mocked contract coverage.
reads.worst: It depends on a paid third-party service and live model schemas, so compatibility and cost remain outside the plugin's control.

reads.best: The complete reading workflow joins a responsive keyboard-and-touch UI with Hermes-managed OAuth, sandboxed email rendering and direct newsletter-to-chat context.
reads.worst: sync() deletes existing Gmail filters before creating replacements and saves their IDs only after all creations succeed, so a partial API failure can break routing or leave untracked filters ([reading_core.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nj07r/hermes-reading/c739110797b0bcd0bad53d8f2a83b8ce1854430d/reading_core.py)).

reads.best: Seven observer hooks, server adapters and an opt-in delegation provider turn local inference visibility into actionable routing, with detailed tests and a finished Desktop view.
reads.worst: At the field-pinned commit, config._read_yaml_config silently returns empty settings when undeclared PyYAML is unavailable, disabling normal server discovery and capacity routing; a later PR fix is outside this pin.

reads.best: Evidence-based fix learning (flaky retries ignored) with egress redaction, signed events, peer quorums and 22 offline tests against a mock relay.
reads.worst: Peer hints go into tool output the agent reads, defended mainly by cheap proof-of-work and a regex blocklist, and the read-mode relay lookup runs synchronously under a lock on the hot path.

reads.best: The local, append-only replay/what-if engine gives Hermes provenance and counterfactual computation over real terminal work, with a substantial demo and product-quality surfaces.
reads.worst: It is a very large and ambitious codebase with PTY execution and many moving parts, so the integration and fidelity failure surface is high even with bundled tests.

reads.best: Character provenance and forward-checked counterfactual edits are an unusual, locally implemented debugging direction.
reads.worst: The bundled bridge rebuilds computations through the tax flagship or coding demo; a generic recorded shell command does not become a recomputable What-if, and a fork only records intent.

reads.best: Plugs in as Hermes's memory provider, with recall-with-sources and versioned corrections.
reads.worst: The catalog folder is an 18-line shim; the real code comes from a pip package outside the pinned folder.

reads.best: Capture, deduplication, time-aware recall and agent-event correlation provide useful memory of screens that have disappeared.
reads.worst: Redaction protects indexed text but not stored screenshots or image attachments, so secrets visible on screen can still reach the model despite the privacy wording.

reads.best: It integrates automatic recall and ingestion through the memory-provider interface, preserves secret scope and includes backend contract and isolation tests.
reads.worst: provider._ingest waits only five seconds for its predecessor before starting another write, while remember permits 120-second requests, contradicting the promised single-in-flight ingestion.

reads.best: A finished visual customization product with import formats, previews, provenance-aware deletion and substantial frontend/backend tests.
reads.worst: Synchronization needs the optional backend and installed transport skins, and native theme painting also reaches outside the plugin SDK through window.hermesDesktop.

reads.best: A substantial app-management interface connects app sessions, marketplace installation and task operations to Hermes.
reads.worst: Remote-app authentication is delegated to a CLI that stores credentials in ~/.a2app/credentials.json instead of Hermes credential routes, and the framework must be installed separately.

reads.best: Deterministic confirmation, capped reminders, sender locking and broad tests make persistent reminders a practical gateway capability.
reads.worst: It depends on private gateway/send surfaces and can consume the first unrelated chat message after a reminder as an invalid answer.

reads.best: It observes real native tool activity and fails closed while preserving clear evidence boundaries rather than trusting model-reported results.
reads.worst: It verifies only criteria a user specifies and is limited to Linux/macOS, so it cannot certify general task completion.

reads.best: Honest scope, read-safety for .env files, descriptor-relative reads and a real test suite.
reads.worst: The bundled catalog yaml is a template with empty repo and sha, and there are no screenshots or demo.

reads.best: Human approval before every send with SMTP/IMAP TLS hardening and 185 tests.
reads.worst: A CRM in a plugin; niche for most Hermes users and large surface area.

reads.best: It offers a deep, evidence-backed release-review workflow with explicit input approvals and clear limits on what static signals and access snapshots establish.
reads.worst: Its scope is specialized to Salesforce and its security and impact results remain human-reviewed heuristics rather than deployment or runtime guarantees.

reads.best: This is a production-minded local testing integration with target/IP fencing, explicit resource caps, secret-scope handling, result comparison, and unit plus real-k6 end-to-end tests.
reads.worst: It requires a separately installed k6 binary and is intentionally constrained to locally reachable or owner-allowlisted targets.

reads.best: Archiving checks recorded bytes and file identity, refuses occupied destinations, and records the destination before moving files so interrupted work remains recoverable [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ladyFaye1998/hermes-clean-exit/1df8501113e5a195fef3794e660ac3839900987f/clean_exit/review.py).
reads.worst: Tracking only observes Windows write_file calls, leaving files produced by shell commands or other editing tools outside its cleanup workflow [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ladyFaye1998/hermes-clean-exit/1df8501113e5a195fef3794e660ac3839900987f/clean_exit/plugin.py).

reads.best: Deterministic budget checks, x402 decoding and an idempotent SQLite receipt ledger are implemented with focused tests.
reads.worst: Default mode only observes, policy errors pass through by default, and recorded spend depends on a separate tool call.

reads.best: The implemented workflow preserves the founder's own words, exposes failed checks, exports usable media, and schedules reminders only after an explicit Yes. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/launch_desk/wizard.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/README.md)
reads.worst: Its niche value depends on posts.design for fresh references and a separate renderer for finished video; deterministic copy checks cannot establish that every prose claim is true. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/launch_desk/wizard.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/README.md)

reads.best: A serious, deterministic guard on self-modifying skills: fail-closed enforce mode, provenance quarantine after untrusted input, sandboxed operator checks, and 340 tests in the repo.
reads.worst: The catalog folder ships only hooks and UI: the caduceus CLI its README tells operators to use (status, release-effect, device-add) lives outside the plugin folder, the folder itself has no tests, and the jargon-heavy docs make it hard to adopt.

reads.best: It checks the Gateway session contract and tier availability before opening a frontend, with bounded RPC/bootstrap waits and real local WebSocket tests.
reads.worst: It depends on recent Hermes Gateway APIs and websockets packaging, is verified live only on macOS, and may leave an empty session if tier validation fails.

reads.best: Simulation, in-memory approvals with a TTL, and an env opt-in gate before execute, plus 16 test files.
reads.worst: Narrow audience and it handles a private key and moves funds, which the catalog reviewer scrutinises heavily.

reads.best: It has a careful quality ladder, write confinement and source-integrity checks, previews, and a broad synthetic test suite.
reads.worst: It is a strong implementation of a familiar document utility rather than a change to Hermes itself.

reads.best: The durable action gateway binds exact arguments to session/task identity, claims execution once and preserves uncertain outcomes for reconciliation.
reads.worst: The first-turn hook can inject owner preferences and people into another participant’s shared-chat turn, while ordinary unscoped calls remain outside PA exact-action enforcement.

reads.best: Placeholder-and-restore design at the llm_request layer keeps PII off providers.
reads.worst: No tests at all, and it downloads a model from Hugging Face at runtime; the HIPAA-style claims go beyond what the code proves.

reads.best: Native session integration includes HMAC and peer checks, explicit owner enrollment, durable replay prevention and a dedicated-process veto on all model tools.
reads.worst: The submitted install subdirectory is only the host plugin; usable hardware firmware, bridge service wiring, enrollment and a clean consumer installation remain external gaps.

reads.best: The implemented pipeline combines configurable frame sampling, local or cloud transcription, persisted segment progress and extensive workbench controls.
reads.worst: Cloud ASR keys are saved in asr-engines.json rather than Hermes secrets, and the pinned repository contains no automated test suite.

reads.best: Its player dock, full page, pop-out, and source-linked show notes make the station convenient while working in Hermes ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-agent-radio-plugin/088a67e1e0bc2f233a1939ab73a80658298be5cd/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: Programming, playback, and moderation depend on a separate station service, leaving the submitted plugin primarily a player and API bridge ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-agent-radio-plugin/088a67e1e0bc2f233a1939ab73a80658298be5cd/__init__.py)).

reads.best: Ten tools with timeouts, caching, fixtures-based tests and screenshots, no keys needed.
reads.worst: Serves a narrow crypto-launchpad audience and is mostly a read-only API wrapper.

reads.best: Adds a real pre-execution review gate without model-callable approval tools or a separate file writer, and tests exact replacements and fail-closed unsupported patches.
reads.worst: _extract_change resolves relative paths against process cwd while the hook discards session context, so its preview may describe a different target; shell writes and opaque patches are not covered.

reads.best: Native provider integration adapts picker capabilities and pricing to the live catalog, with scoped secrets and bounded image handling.
reads.worst: No tests are shipped, and the paid-model setting filters the picker rather than preventing a directly selected paid model from being requested.

reads.best: Supply chain handled with care: the release tarball is refused unless its sha256 matches a pinned table, and the VLLM key is read only via get_secret and never minted without an explicit terms step.
reads.worst: The plugin itself is a thin installer with no tests of its own that fetches and runs 16.5 MB of native binaries, and its visual checks depend on a third-party Decision API key; DOS automation is a narrow audience.

reads.best: Implements transactional proposal application, stable history, exact source-quote checks, stale-write protection and contained exports, with substantive persistence and concurrency tests.
reads.worst: Extraction and approval still depend on the model following the workflow: apply is directly callable, and the reported guided demo required corrections to inferred commitments and deadline handling.

reads.best: The package is unusually candid about hosted logging, stale observations, quotas, terms, and read-only behavior.
reads.worst: Most of the capability is a remote service; the Hermes contribution is a thin MCP connection and skill around a narrow audience.

reads.best: Marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before non-read-only tools, with pinned mcp-remote and OAuth sign-in.
reads.worst: No code or tests of its own; essentially a wrapper for a paid SaaS, and OAuth tokens live in ~/.mcp-auth outside Hermes's secret store.

reads.best: Inventive agent-as-VLM review loop with a recorded end-to-end demo.
reads.worst: 84-line wrapper with no tests that relies on an uninstalled upstream package and ffmpeg; README mostly Chinese.

reads.best: Direct crypt32 integration, explicit pointer signatures and unit/live test cases give useful diagnostics without shell parsing or elevation.
reads.worst: The self_signed field only compares subject and issuer names, so it does not verify that a certificate actually signed itself.

reads.best: Corroborated verdicts distinguish a live gateway socket from stale state files, with time-bounded probes and tests for misleading or malformed evidence.
reads.worst: Recovery executes SSH mutations based on model-set dry_run and confirm flags rather than a Hermes approval prompt, and the PR description disagrees with the pinned implementation about storage and restart behavior.

reads.best: Money-moving tools are gated behind Hermes approval through a pre_tool_call hook.
reads.worst: Signing seed is kept in a plain JSON file rather than the secret store, there are no tests and no README in the plugin folder.

reads.best: Full TypeScript source alongside the bundle, redacted errors, and a three-OS CI matrix that builds and smoke-tests the server.
reads.worst: It is not a Hermes-native plugin and takes its credentials from the Grok CLI's ~/.grok/auth.json file instead of Hermes's secret store, spends paid xAI quota with no approval gate, and its local UI server has no auth.

reads.best: Fixes a real annoyance with a status chip and confirmation before releasing live owners.
reads.worst: Edits Hermes runtime files directly, ships a Windows-only installer and its one test file has no test functions.

reads.best: It is honest and safe: the server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before non-read-only tools, and the key comes from the Hermes env.
reads.worst: No local code or tests; it is a marketing-analytics vendor's skills and MCP endpoint, useful mainly to DevTune customers.

reads.best: The documentation clearly explains account limits, profile-owned authentication, source freshness and approval expectations for remote actions [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koala73/worldmonitor-hermes-plugin/8db8fb2f5ea71d464c2f380a7c8564868c678986/README.md).
reads.worst: The pinned contribution adds only remote MCP configuration and skill guidance, with Hermes installation and authenticated interoperability explicitly unverified [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koala73/worldmonitor-hermes-plugin/8db8fb2f5ea71d464c2f380a7c8564868c678986/README.md).

reads.best: Local rendering, emotion and size validation, bundled assets and rendering tests make the narrow feature tangible.
reads.worst: Imports Pillow unconditionally without declaring a Python dependency, and the claimed automatic emotional reactions have no registered detection hook.

reads.best: Deterministic before/after scoring keeps the rewrite checkable.
reads.worst: Thin client for a metered paid service; no tests, and the transform_tool_result hook touches every post-like tool result.

reads.best: Clear README and OAuth sign-in without pasting keys.
reads.worst: No plugin code at all, just an MCP config and skills for a vendor's hosted service.

reads.best: The single read-only tool validates addresses and provides a compact set of on-chain facts without signing or keys.
reads.worst: A nonstandard token string can abort the whole inspection rather than leave optional metadata unknown; serial public-RPC fallbacks can make a check very slow.

reads.best: The underlying game concept (agents playing a persistent MMO, 'Humans vs AI war') is a creative idea, and the README is transparent about its limited scope and risks.
reads.worst: By its own admission ('There is no executable code and nothing that downloads or updates itself') this is just an MCP passthrough plus a skill file — all logic lives on a third party's server, so a skill/MCP config alone could reproduce it, and it runs game actions including attacks on other players without per-action approval by default.

reads.best: Simple MCP config marked untrusted, with a no-key sandbox.
reads.worst: There is no code; the endpoint in mcp.json (api.qrblox.com/mcp/v1) differs from the one in the README (app.qrblox.com/api/mcp), and it is a vendor advert.

reads.best: It is a clearly documented, read-only connector with a simple public-data scope.
reads.worst: The README says the hosted endpoint is still launching and may not answer, and the pinned package has no implementation or tests.

reads.best: Honest and harmless: the PR and manifest say it is skill only, with no tools, hooks, network or env.
reads.worst: It is a product advertisement for a paid third-party app delivered as a skill; a prompt or skill does exactly the same and there is no code doing work.
